But now we have to prove the connection between the man and the beast. Save from what we heard, we cannot even swear to the existence of the latter, since Sir Henry has evidently died from the fall. But, by heavens, cunning as he is, the fellow shall be in my power before another day is past!

events.label: Watson and Holmes stand by the body and grieve over the disaster
Watson suggests seizing Stapleton at once and Holmes rejects it as premature

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Why should we not seize him at once?

events.label: Watson and Holmes go down the slope to the body to perform the last offices

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: We must send for help, Holmes! We cannot carry him all the way to the Hall.

events.label: Holmes inspects the body, cries out, laughs, and identifies a beard

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: A beard! A beard! The man has a beard! A beard? It is not the baronet—it is—why, it is my neighbour, the convict!

events.label: Watson recognizes the body as Selden and realizes the clothing is Sir Henry's

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I told Holmes how the matter stood, my heart bubbling over with thankfulness and joy.

events.label: A speaker states that the clothes have been the poor devil's death

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Then the clothes have been the poor devil’s death.

events.label: A speaker states that the hound was laid on from Sir Henry's boot and ran Selden down

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It is clear enough that the hound has been laid on from some article of Sir Henry’s—the boot which was abstracted in the hotel, in all probability—and so ran this man down.

events.label: A speaker asks how Selden knew the hound was on his trail in the darkness

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: How came Selden, in the darkness, to know that the hound was on his trail?

events.label: A speaker replies that Selden heard the hound

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: He heard him.

events.label: A speaker argues that hearing a hound would not usually terrify Selden into screaming for help

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: To hear a hound upon the moor would not work a hard man like this convict into such a paroxysm of terror that he would risk recapture by screaming wildly for help. By his cries he must have run a long way after he knew the animal was on his track. How did he know?

events.label: A speaker says the hound should be loose tonight and suggests Stapleton let it go for Sir Henry's presence

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: A greater mystery to me is why this hound, presuming that all our conjectures are correct—Well, then, why this hound should be loose tonight. I suppose that it does not always run loose upon the moor. Stapleton would not let it go unless he had reason to think that Sir Henry would be there.

events.label: A speaker says that they will likely soon get an explanation of one mystery while another may remain a mystery

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My difficulty is the more formidable of the two, for I think that we shall very shortly get an explanation of yours, while mine may remain forever a mystery.

events.label: A speaker asks what to do with Selden's body

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The question now is, what shall we do with this poor wretch’s body? We cannot leave it here to the foxes and the ravens.

events.label: A speaker suggests putting the body in a hut until the police can be contacted

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I suggest that we put it in one of the huts until we can communicate with the police.

events.label: A speaker agrees and says they could carry the body that far

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Exactly. I have no doubt that you and I could carry it so far.

events.label: Stapleton approaches over the moor with a cigar
Holmes tells Watson not to reveal suspicions

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Not a word to show your suspicions—not a word, or my plans crumble to the ground.

events.label: Stapleton greets Watson and asks about the body

communicates.speaker: stapleton
communicates.content: Why, Dr. Watson, that’s not you, is it? You are the last man that I should have expected to see out on the moor at this time of night. But, dear me, what’s this? Somebody hurt? Not—don’t tell me that it is our friend Sir Henry!

events.label: Stapleton stoops over the dead man and drops his cigar
Stapleton asks who the dead man is

communicates.speaker: stapleton
communicates.content: Who—who’s this?

events.label: Holmes identifies the dead man as Selden, the escaped convict

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It is Selden, the man who escaped from Princetown.

events.label: Stapleton reacts and asks how Selden died

communicates.speaker: stapleton
communicates.content: Dear me! What a very shocking affair! How did he die?

events.label: Holmes says Selden appears to have broken his neck by falling over the rocks and explains hearing a cry while strolling on the moor

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: He appears to have broken his neck by falling over these rocks. My friend and I were strolling on the moor when we heard a cry.

events.label: Stapleton says he also heard a cry and came out because he was uneasy about Sir Henry

communicates.speaker: stapleton
communicates.content: I heard a cry also. That was what brought me out. I was uneasy about Sir Henry.

events.label: Stapleton explains that he had suggested Sir Henry come over and that he became alarmed when he heard cries upon the moor

communicates.speaker: stapleton
communicates.content: Because I had suggested that he should come over. When he did not come I was surprised, and I naturally became alarmed for his safety when I heard cries upon the moor.

events.label: Stapleton asks whether anything else was heard besides a cry and says he wondered about evidence of a phantom hound

communicates.speaker: stapleton
communicates.content: By the way—did you hear anything else besides a cry? No. What do you mean, then? Oh, you know the stories that the peasants tell about a phantom hound, and so on. It is said to be heard at night upon the moor. I was wondering if there were any evidence of such a sound tonight.

events.label: I says nothing of the kind

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: We heard nothing of the kind.

events.label: A speaker asks Holmes for a theory of the man's death

communicates.speaker: mr_stapleton
communicates.content: And what is your theory of this poor fellow's death?

events.label: A speaker explains a theory of the death

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I have no doubt that anxiety and exposure have driven him off his head. He has rushed about the moor in a crazy state and eventually fallen over here and broken his neck.

events.label: Stapleton agrees that the theory seems reasonable

communicates.speaker: mr_stapleton
communicates.content: That seems the most reasonable theory.

events.label: Holmes is asked for his view

communicates.speaker: mr_stapleton
communicates.content: What do you think about it, Mr. Sherlock Holmes?

events.label: Holmes bows his compliments
Holmes identifies the speaker quickly

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You are quick at identification.

events.label: Holmes says he and Watson had been expected in the area

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We have been expecting you in these parts since Dr. Watson came down. You are in time to see a tragedy.

events.label: Holmes says he will return to London tomorrow

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Yes, indeed. I have no doubt that my friend's explanation will cover the facts. I will take an unpleasant remembrance back to London with me tomorrow.

events.label: Stapleton asks whether Holmes returns tomorrow

communicates.speaker: mr_stapleton
communicates.content: Oh, you return tomorrow?

events.label: Holmes says that returning tomorrow is his intention

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: That is my intention.

events.label: Stapleton asks whether the visit has shed light on the occurrences

communicates.speaker: mr_stapleton
communicates.content: I hope your visit has cast some light upon those occurrences which have puzzled us?

events.label: Holmes answers that he cannot always succeed and that the case has not been satisfactory

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: One cannot always have the success for which one hopes. An investigator needs facts and not legends or rumours. It has not been a satisfactory case.

events.label: Stapleton turns to Watson
Stapleton proposes carrying the body to his house and covering the face until morning

communicates.speaker: mr_stapleton
communicates.content: I would suggest carrying this poor fellow to my house, but it would give my sister such a fright that I do not feel justified in doing it. I think that if we put something over his face he will be safe until morning.

events.label: Holmes and Watson set off for Baskerville Hall
Holmes and Watson see Stapleton return alone over the moor
Holmes says they are at close grips at last

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We're at close grips at last.

events.label: Holmes says the fellow showed nerve and the wrong man fell victim to his plot

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: What a nerve the fellow has! How he pulled himself together in the face of what must have been a paralyzing shock when he found that the wrong man had fallen a victim to his plot. I told you in London, Watson, and I tell you now again, that we have never had a foeman more worthy of our steel.

events.label: Watson says he is sorry that Holmes has been seen

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: I am sorry that he has seen you.

events.label: Holmes says he was sorry at first but could not avoid being seen

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And so was I at first. But there was no getting out of it.

events.label: Watson asks what effect Holmes's presence will have on the man's plans

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: What effect do you think it will have upon his plans now that he knows you are here?

events.label: Holmes says the man's response may be caution or desperate action

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: It may cause him to be more cautious, or it may drive him to desperate measures at once. Like most clever criminals, he may be too confident in his own cleverness and imagine that he has completely deceived us.

events.label: Watson asks why they should not arrest the man at once

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Why should we not arrest him at once?

events.label: Holmes says Watson is a man of action and that arresting the man tonight would not help

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear Watson, you were born to be a man of action. Your instinct is always to do something energetic. But supposing, for argument's sake, that we had him arrested tonight, what on earth the better off should we be for that? We could prove nothing against him. There’s the devilish cunning of it! If he were acting through a human agent we could get some evidence, but if we were to drag this great dog to the light of day it would not help us in putting a rope round the neck of its master.

events.label: Watson says they have a case

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: Surely we have a case.

events.label: Holmes says they have only surmise and conjecture and would be laughed out of court

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Not a shadow of one—only surmise and conjecture. We should be laughed out of court if we came with such a story and such evidence.

events.label: Holmes and Watson discuss Sir Charles's death and the lack of proof

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There is Sir Charles’s death. Found dead without a mark upon him. But we have to prove all this, and we are not in a position to do it.

events.label: Holmes says they cannot prove the hound caused Sir Charles's death

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Found dead without a mark upon him. You and I know that he died of sheer fright, and we know also what frightened him, but how are we to get twelve stolid jurymen to know it? Of course we know that a hound does not bite a dead body and that Sir Charles was dead before ever the brute overtook him.

events.label: Holmes says there is no direct proof connecting the hound to the death

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: We are not much better off tonight. Again, there was no direct connection between the hound and the man’s death. We never saw the hound. We heard it, but we could not prove that it was running upon this man’s trail. There is a complete absence of motive. No, my dear fellow; we must reconcile ourselves to the fact that we have no case at present, and that it is worth our while to run any risk in order to establish one.

events.label: Holmes says Mrs. Laura Lyons may help them and that he has another plan

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have great hopes of what Mrs. Laura Lyons may do for us when the position of affairs is made clear to her. And I have my own plan as well. Sufficient for tomorrow is the evil thereof; but I hope before the day is past to have the upper hand at last.

events.label: Holmes and Watson walk to the Baskerville gates

communicates.speaker: narrator
communicates.content: I could draw nothing further from him, and he walked, lost in thought, as far as the Baskerville gates.

events.label: Holmes tells Watson not to mention the hound to Sir Henry

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Yes; I see no reason for further concealment. But one last word, Watson. Say nothing of the hound to Sir Henry. Let him think that Selden’s death was as Stapleton would have us believe. He will have a better nerve for the ordeal which he will have to undergo tomorrow, when he is engaged, if I remember your report aright, to dine with these people.

events.label: Watson says he is also engaged to dine with those people

communicates.speaker: watson
communicates.content: And so am I.

events.label: Holmes says Watson must excuse himself and Sir Henry must go alone to dinner

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Then you must excuse yourself and he must go alone. That will be easily arranged. And now, if we are too late for dinner, I think that we are both ready for our suppers.

events.label: Sir Henry sees Sherlock Holmes arrive
Sir Henry notices Holmes has no luggage and no explanation for it
Watson and Holmes explain their experience to Sir Henry over a belated supper

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: as much of our experience as it seemed desirable that he should know

events.label: Watson breaks the news to Barrymore and his wife

communicates.speaker: dr_watson
communicates.content: the news

events.label: Mrs. Barrymore weeps
Sir Henry says he has been moping in the house since Watson left

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: I’ve been moping in the house all day since Watson went off in the morning

events.label: Sir Henry says he kept his promise

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: I guess I should have some credit, for I have kept my promise

events.label: Sir Henry says Stapleton sent him a message asking him to come over

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: If I hadn’t sworn not to go about alone I might have had a more lively evening, for I had a message from Stapleton asking me over there

events.label: Holmes says they had been mourning Sir Henry as having broken his neck

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I don’t suppose you appreciate that we have been mourning over you as having broken your neck?

events.label: Holmes identifies the dead man as dressed in Sir Henry's clothes

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: This poor wretch was dressed in your clothes. I fear your servant who gave them to him may get into trouble with the police.

events.label: Holmes says the household is on the wrong side of the law and Watson's reports are incriminating

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: That’s lucky for him—in fact, it’s lucky for all of you, since you are all on the wrong side of the law in this matter. I am not sure that as a conscientious detective my first duty is not to arrest the whole household. Watson’s reports are most incriminating documents.

events.label: Sir Henry asks Holmes about the case

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: But how about the case? Have you made anything out of the tangle? I don’t know that Watson and I are much the wiser since we came down.

events.label: Holmes says he will soon make the situation clearer

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I think that I shall be in a position to make the situation rather more clear to you before long. It has been an exceedingly difficult and most complicated business. There are several points upon which we still want light—but it is coming all the same.

events.label: Sir Henry says they heard the hound on the moor

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: We’ve had one experience, as Watson has no doubt told you. We heard the hound on the moor, so I can swear that it is not all empty superstition. I had something to do with dogs when I was out West, and I know one when I hear one. If you can muzzle that one and put him on a chain I’ll be ready to swear you are the greatest detective of all time.

events.label: Holmes says he will muzzle and chain the hound if Sir Henry helps

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I think I will muzzle him and chain him all right if you will give me your help.

events.label: Sir Henry agrees to do whatever Holmes tells him

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: Whatever you tell me to do I will do. Just as you like.

events.label: Holmes asks Sir Henry to obey blindly without asking the reason

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Very good; and I will ask you also to do it blindly, without always asking the reason.

events.label: Holmes abruptly looks and stares upward
Holmes admires the portraits on the opposite wall

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Excuse the admiration of a connoisseur.

events.label: Holmes identifies the family portraits by name and ancestry

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: That’s a Kneller, I’ll swear, that lady in the blue silk over yonder, and the stout gentleman with the wig ought to be a Reynolds. They are all family portraits, I presume? That is Rear-Admiral Baskerville ... The man with the blue coat and the roll of paper is Sir William Baskerville ... That is the cause of all the mischief, the wicked Hugo, who started the Hound of the Baskervilles.

events.label: Barrymore coaches Sir Henry in the names of the portraits

communicates.speaker: barrymore
communicates.content: Barrymore has been coaching me in them.

events.label: Holmes examines the portrait during supper
Holmes returns to the banqueting-hall with a candle and inspects the portrait
Holmes reveals Stapleton's face in the portrait

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Do you see anything there? Is it like anyone you know? Just a suggestion, perhaps. But wait an instant! ... My eyes have been trained to examine faces and not their trimmings. It is the first quality of a criminal investigator that he should see through a disguise.

events.label: Holmes identifies the Baskerville man as having designs on the succession and says he will be trapped soon

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Yes, it is an interesting instance of a throwback, which appears to be both physical and spiritual. A study of family portraits is enough to convert a man to the doctrine of reincarnation. The fellow is a Baskerville—that is evident. With designs upon the succession. Exactly. This chance of the picture has supplied us with one of our most obvious missing links. We have him, Watson, we have him, and I dare swear that before tomorrow night he will be fluttering in our net as helpless as one of his own butterflies. A pin, a cork, and a card, and we add him to the Baker Street collection!

events.label: Holmes laughs and turns away from the portrait
Holmes arrives earlier in the morning and speaks with Watson

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Yes, we should have a full day today. The nets are all in place, and the drag is about to begin. We’ll know before the day is out whether we have caught our big, lean-jawed pike, or whether he has got through the meshes.

events.label: Holmes reports Selden's death to Princetown and reassures Cartwright

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have sent a report from Grimpen to Princetown as to the death of Selden. I think I can promise that none of you will be troubled in the matter. And I have also communicated with my faithful Cartwright, who would certainly have pined away at the door of my hut, as a dog does at his master’s grave, if I had not set his mind at rest about my safety.

events.label: Holmes says the next move is to see Sir Henry

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: To see Sir Henry. Ah, here he is!

events.label: Sir Henry greets Holmes and discusses the day's plan

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: Good-morning, Holmes. You look like a general who is planning a battle with his chief of the staff. And so do I. I hoped that you were going to see me through this business. The Hall and the moor are not very pleasant places when one is alone. I hope that you will come also. They are very hospitable people, and I am sure that they would be very glad to see you. I fear that Watson and I must go to London. To London? Yes, I think that we should be more useful there at the present juncture.

events.label: Sir Henry feels hurt by the planned departure
Holmes instructs Sir Henry to trust him, relay an excuse to the Stapletons, and remember the message

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My dear fellow, you must trust me implicitly and do exactly what I tell you. You can tell your friends that we should have been happy to have come with you, but that urgent business required us to be in town. We hope very soon to return to Devonshire. Will you remember to give them that message? If you insist upon it. There is no alternative, I assure you.

events.label: Holmes and Watson plan to leave immediately after breakfast and travel to Coombe Tracey, while Watson leaves his things as a pledge

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Immediately after breakfast. We will drive in to Coombe Tracey, but Watson will leave his things as a pledge that he will come back to you. Watson, you will send a note to Stapleton to tell him that you regret that you cannot come.

events.label: Sir Henry says he wants to go to London and not stay alone at the Hall

communicates.speaker: sir_henry_baskerville
communicates.content: I have a good mind to go to London with you. Why should I stay here alone?

events.label: Holmes sends a report from Grimpen to Princetown about Selden's death
Holmes communicates with Cartwright about his safety
Holmes orders Watson to stay and gives further travel instructions

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: Because it is your post of duty. Because you gave me your word that you would do as you were told, and I tell you to stay. One more direction! I wish you to drive to Merripit House. Send back your trap, however, and let them know that you intend to walk home. Yes. This time you may do it with safety. If I had not every confidence in your nerve and courage I would not suggest it, but it is essential that you should do it. And as you value your life do not go across the moor in any direction save along the straight path which leads from Merripit House to the Grimpen Road, and is your natural way home. Very good. I should be glad to get away as soon after breakfast as possible, so as to reach London in the afternoon.

events.label: Holmes, Watson, and their companion travel to Coombe Tracey and send the trap back

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There was nothing for it, however, but implicit obedience; so we bade good-bye to our rueful friend, and a couple of hours afterwards we were at the station of Coombe Tracey and had dispatched the trap upon its return journey.

events.label: Holmes instructs Cartwright to wire Sir Henry and check for a station message

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: You will take this train to town, Cartwright. The moment you arrive you will send a wire to Sir Henry Baskerville, in my name, to say that if he finds the pocketbook which I have dropped he is to send it by registered post to Baker Street. And ask at the station office if there is a message for me.

events.label: Cartwright returns with a telegram and Holmes reads it to Watson

communicates.speaker: the_telegraph_answer
communicates.content: Wire received. Coming down with unsigned warrant. Arrive five-forty. Lestrade.

events.label: Holmes states that Lestrade is the best professional and that they may need his help

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: That is in answer to mine of this morning. He is the best of the professionals, I think, and we may need his assistance.

events.label: Holmes proposes calling on Mrs. Laura Lyons

communicates.speaker: holmes
communicates.content: Now, Watson, I think that we cannot employ our time better than by calling upon your acquaintance, Mrs. Laura Lyons.

events.label: Holmes explains his campaign and the use of Sir Henry and the telegram
Holmes interviews Mrs. Laura Lyons in her office

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I am investigating the circumstances which attended the death of the late Sir Charles Baskerville.

events.label: Holmes says Watson has informed him of what Mrs. Laura Lyons communicated and withheld about Sir Charles's death

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: My friend here, Dr. Watson, has informed me of what you have communicated, and also of what you have withheld in connection with that matter.

events.label: Mrs. Laura Lyons asks what she has withheld

communicates.speaker: mrs_laura_lyons
communicates.content: What have I withheld?

events.label: Holmes states that Mrs. Laura Lyons asked Sir Charles to be at the gate at ten o'clock and that this was the place and hour of his death

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: You have confessed that you asked Sir Charles to be at the gate at ten o'clock. We know that that was the place and hour of his death. You have withheld what the connection is between these events.

events.label: Holmes denies that there is any connection

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: There is no connection. In that case the coincidence must indeed be an extraordinary one. But I think that we shall succeed in establishing a connection, after all.

events.label: Holmes states that the case is treated as murder and that evidence may implicate Mr. Stapleton and his wife

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I wish to be perfectly frank with you, Mrs. Lyons. We regard this case as one of murder, and the evidence may implicate not only your friend Mr. Stapleton but his wife as well.

events.label: Mrs. Lyons reacts by springing from her chair and crying out

communicates.speaker: mrs_lyons
communicates.content: His wife!

events.label: Holmes states that the supposed sister is really the man's wife

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: The fact is no longer a secret. The person who has passed for his sister is really his wife.

events.label: Mrs. Lyons resumes her seat and grips the chair arms
Mrs. Lyons demands proof that Mr. Stapleton is married

communicates.speaker: mrs_lyons
communicates.content: His wife! His wife! He is not a married man.

events.label: Holmes produces papers as proof

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I have come prepared to do so. Here is a photograph of the couple taken in York four years ago. It is indorsed ‘Mr. and Mrs. Vandeleur,’ but you will have no difficulty in recognizing him, and her also, if you know her by sight. Here are three written descriptions by trustworthy witnesses of Mr. and Mrs. Vandeleur, who at that time kept St. Oliver’s private school. Read them and see if you can doubt the identity of these people.

events.label: Mrs. Lyons accuses the man of lying and of using her as a tool

communicates.speaker: mrs_lyons
communicates.content: Mr. Holmes, this man had offered me marriage on condition that I could get a divorce from my husband. He has lied to me, the villain, in every conceivable way. Not one word of truth has he ever told me. And why—why? I imagined that all was for my own sake. But now I see that I was never anything but a tool in his hands. Why should I preserve faith with him who never kept any with me? Why should I try to shield him from the consequences of his own wicked acts? Ask me what you like, and there is nothing which I shall hold back. One thing I swear to you, and that is that when I wrote the letter I never dreamed of any harm to the old gentleman, who had been my kindest friend.

events.label: Holmes says he believes Mrs. Lyons and asks about the letter and the appointment

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I entirely believe you, madam. The recital of these events must be very painful to you, and perhaps it will make it easier if I tell you what occurred, and you can check me if I make any material mistake. The sending of this letter was suggested to you by Stapleton?

events.label: Mrs. Lyons says Stapleton dictated the letter

communicates.speaker: mrs_lyons
communicates.content: He dictated it.

events.label: Holmes asks about the reason given for the letter

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: I presume that the reason he gave was that you would receive help from Sir Charles for the legal expenses connected with your divorce?

events.label: Mrs. Lyons confirms the reason for the letter

communicates.speaker: mrs_lyons
communicates.content: Exactly.

events.label: Holmes asks whether Stapleton dissuaded her from keeping the appointment

communicates.speaker: sherlock_holmes
communicates.content: And then after you had sent the letter he dissuaded you from keeping the appointment?
